practice: Standards are a checklist, not a wish list
rule: Treat the team's written standards as a checklist every change must meet, not as aspirations.
why: Warna rules sirf kaghaz par rehte hain aur har repo ka code alag shakal le leta hai.

practice: Small approved stack, decisions for additions
rule: Build new projects from a short list of approved frameworks, and add new tech only with a short written decision record.
why: Har project mein naya framework aur bina soche dependencies stack ko bikhar dete hain.

rule: Prioritize long term code health over how fast the first version ships.
why: Jaldi mein likha code baad mein har change ko slow aur risky bana deta hai.

rule: Choose the simplest solution that meets today's requirement, not an imagined future one.
why: Aisi cheezein banane se bachte hain jo kabhi use nahi hongi magar maintain karni parti hain.

rule: Deliver the required outcome with the fewest new abstractions, contracts, modes and persistent state.
why: Har nayi abstraction ya contract ka bojh hamesha ke liye uthana parta hai.

rule: Make intent clear through code structure and names rather than hidden conventions or magic.
why: Chupi hui behaviour se naye developer ko bugs aur ghalat fehmi hoti hai.

rule: Apply full production rigor (tests, review, CI, migration discipline) as soon as real users or real data are involved.
why: Practice project mein bhi bad habits ban jati hain jo production mein nuqsan karti hain.

rule: Learn numeric defaults such as 40 line functions and 400 line files first, then learn when the logic justifies an exception.
why: Beginner ko wazeh had chahiye, warna "depends" ke naam par sab kuch bara hota jata hai.

rule: Do not write explanatory comments or docblocks; rename, extract a function or add a named constant instead.
why: Comments purane ho kar jhoot bolne lagte hain jabke naam code ke saath badalte hain.

rule: Keep comments only for machine directives such as lint pragmas, codegen markers, API doc generators and migration headers.
why: Is se exceptions ki list chhoti aur wazeh rehti hai, aur comments wapas nahi phailte.

rule: Remove unused code instead of commenting it out; version control already keeps the history.
why: Commented code se file ganda hota hai aur log samajh nahi pate ke yeh zaroori hai ya nahi.

rule: Replace hard to read inline conditions with named predicates such as isExpired, and name functions for what they do, not how.
why: Reader ko condition decode nahi karni parti, naam khud matlab bata deta hai.

rule: Name functions with one short verb such as dispatch, plan or record instead of a long phrase.
why: Lambe naam code ko bhaari banate hain aur aksar function ke do kaam chhupate hain.

rule: Use full descriptive words from the problem domain; single letters only for loop counters and abbreviations only when the domain uses them.
why: Khud ke banaye short forms aur ek harf wale naam doosre developers ke liye paheli ban jate hain.

rule: Prefix booleans with is, has, can or should, for example isExpired or canEdit.
why: Bina prefix ke yeh pata nahi chalta ke value true/false hai ya koi aur cheez.

practice: Consistent file names and named exports
rule: Use one file naming convention per folder and named exports everywhere except where the framework requires a default.
why: Mixed naming aur default exports se imports guessing game aur refactor mushkil ban jate hain.

rule: Every if, else, for and while uses full braces, even for a single statement, with the body never on the condition line.
why: Brace ke baghair nayi line add karne par logic chupke se toot jata hai.

rule: Use guard clauses and early returns to keep the main path unindented, unless nesting mirrors a domain decision more clearly.
why: Gehri nesting mein asal logic dhoondna mushkil ho jata hai.

rule: Write if (!x) rather than comparing to null unless the difference between null, undefined and falsy actually matters.
why: Faltu lambi checks code ko shor bana deti hain.

rule: Use if/else or an early return instead of the cond ? a : b operator.
why: Ternary chains jaldi ulajh jati hain aur debug karna mushkil hota hai.

rule: In returned JSX use neither ternaries nor &&; call a small render function with a braced guard such as {renderBanner()}.
why: JSX ke andar conditions markup ko parhna mushkil aur bugs (jaise 0 render hona) paida karti hain.

practice: Nullish operator only for optional values
rule: Use ?? only to default genuinely optional values, and expand value ?? throw into an explicit null check and throw.
why: Default value missing data ka bug chhupa deti hai aur ek line ka throw control flow chhupata hai.

rule: Keep a function under 40 lines and under 20 where possible, splitting by responsibility rather than by line count alone.
why: Lamba function kai kaam karta hai aur test aur samajhna dono mushkil hote hain.

rule: If describing a function or component needs the word and, split it.
why: Do kaam wala unit dono mein se kisi ek ke change par toot jata hai.

rule: Keep each function at a single level of abstraction; extract lower level details into named helpers.
why: High aur low level baatein mix hon to function ka maqsad samajh nahi aata.

rule: Prefer pure functions and keep data transformation separate from side effects.
why: Pure code test karna aasan hai aur side effects ek jagah control mein rehte hain.

rule: Keep a component file under 400 lines; past that, split it into child components in their own files.
why: Bari component file mein state aur markup ka jungle ban jata hai.

rule: Give each file one primary responsibility, keep related code together, and split only when parts change for independent reasons.
why: Mixed files mein cheez dhoondna aur safely badalna mushkil hota hai.

rule: Place a component or module in its own folder with its types file, and nest private children under it.
why: Har cheez ek predictable jagah par hoti hai, dhoondna aur move karna aasan.

rule: Extract duplicated logic the second time it appears, not the third.
why: Teesri copy tak pohanchte pohanchte copies alag alag drift kar chuki hoti hain.

rule: Merge only code that is one idea changing in one place, and prefer a small shared function over an abstraction controlled by flags.
why: Ghalat abstraction do alag cheezon ko zabardasti baandh deti hai aur flags se ulajhti jati hai.

rule: Search existing code for a function that already does the job before writing a new one, and say in the pull request what was reused.
why: Near-duplicate functions waqt ke saath alag behave karne lagte hain.

rule: Build a variant of a component as a prop or option on the base, never as a copied file.
why: Copied components drift karte hain aur har fix do baar karna parta hai.

rule: Do not write ?? {} or ?? [] for values the contract guarantees; when required data is missing, throw.
why: Fallback asal producer ka bug chhupa deta hai aur ghalat data aage chala jata hai.

rule: Detect and report errors as early as possible, close to their cause.
why: Der se pakra gaya error apni asal wajah se door ho kar debug ko lamba kar deta hai.

rule: No empty catch blocks; handle an error, log it with context, or propagate it.
why: Nigla hua error system ko ghalat state mein chalta chhor deta hai.

rule: Validate config in one module at boot and register routes explicitly, so a missing value or broken file stops startup.
why: Chupke se skip hua route ya missing setting production mein beech raste crash karta hai.

rule: Separate logic blocks with a single blank line and always leave a blank line before return.
why: Ek ghana paragraph jaisa code parhna mushkil hota hai.

rule: Inline a value assigned and used once; name only reused values, accumulators and predicates.
why: Faltu variables reader ko upar neeche jump karwate hain.

rule: Use one formatter config per repo plus spacing lint rules, and check both in CI.
why: Formatting par review mein behas khatam hoti hai aur diffs saaf rehte hain.

rule: Extract unexplained literals into named constants.
why: Akela number ya string yeh nahi batata ke woh kyun hai aur kahan kahan use hai.

rule: Represent statuses, limits and keys as enums or const objects, and read stored state through typed accessors, not magic strings.
why: Spelling ki ek ghalti silent bug ban jati hai.

rule: Keep user-facing message strings as constants so tests assert the same constant the code returns.
why: Message badalne par test aur code dono ek saath update rehte hain.

rule: Refactor one small change at a time and run the tests after each step.
why: Bara refactor ek saath karne par toot phoot ka source dhoondna mushkil hota hai.

rule: Refactor related code only when it lowers the risk or cost of the current change, and report other cleanup separately.
why: Scope se bahar ka cleanup unrelated bugs aur bare diffs lata hai.

practice: Delete obsolete code after checking callers
rule: Remove code the change made obsolete only after confirming nothing else calls it.
why: Bina check kiye delete karna kisi aur feature ko tor sakta hai.

rule: Enable the compiler's strict mode in every TypeScript project from the first commit.
why: Strict ke baghair bohat se null aur type bugs runtime tak pohanch jate hain.

rule: Do not use any, unchecked casts or leftover type-error suppressions.
why: Any type system ko band kar deta hai aur bugs chhup jate hain.

rule: Parse external input into a typed shape at the entry point with a step that fails loudly, instead of casting.
why: Cast jhooti tasalli deta hai aur ghalat data chupke se andar chala jata hai.

practice: Types in a sibling types file
rule: Put a module's types, interfaces and constants in a .types.ts file next to it; the logic file imports them and never declares them.
why: Logic file saaf rehti hai aur types ek jagah hon to duplicate shapes nahi bante.

rule: Keep a module, its types file and an optional pure-helpers file together in a folder named for the module, and nothing else.
why: Har module ki shakal ek jaisi ho to naya developer fauran rasta pa leta hai.

practice: All business logic lives in services
rule: Every calculation, state transition, permission decision and query belongs in a service module, never in a controller, page or component.
why: Controller ya UI mein logic ho to dobara use aur test karna mushkil ho jata hai.

rule: A controller action validates input, calls one service function and returns one response helper, with no helper functions in the file.
why: Chhota handler review mein auth aur validation ek nazar mein dikhata hai.

rule: Service functions take plain arguments, never request or context objects, so routes, jobs, scripts and tests call them the same way.
why: Framework types service ko sirf HTTP tak qaid kar dete hain.

practice: Wrap third-party providers in a service
rule: Isolate payment and other vendor SDK calls behind a service module, never called directly from routes or components.
why: Vendor badalne ya uska bug fix karne ke liye poora code nahi chhoona parta.

rule: Keep domain logic, data access and presentation in separate units; a component that fetches, transforms and renders is three things.
why: Layers mix hon to UI change par database code toot jata hai.

rule: A hook returns a named object such as { leads, isLoading, refresh }, never a positional tuple and never JSX.
why: Positional tuple mein order ki ghalti aasan hai aur JSX return karna concerns mix karta hai.

practice: Pages compose, they do not compute
rule: Routes and screens compose feature components; they do not fetch data or run calculations themselves.
why: Page mein logic ho to woh reuse aur test nahi hota.

rule: Use import restriction lint rules so a pure domain layer cannot import framework or vendor code.
why: Boundary sirf naseehat ho to waqt ke saath toot jati hai.

rule: Pass external dependencies in through constructor or function parameters so tests can substitute them.
why: Hard-wired dependencies test mein replace nahi ho sakti.

rule: Depend on interfaces rather than concrete implementations and keep dependencies between modules few.
why: Concrete dependency se implementation badalna poore code ko hila deta hai.

rule: Prefer a static factory such as Foo.make() over new Foo() at call sites so construction rules live in one place.
why: Object banane ka tareeqa badle to sirf ek jagah change karna parta hai.

rule: The README explains what this product is and how to run it; delete starter READMEs and unused template code on day one.
why: Template leftovers naye developer ko ghalat raste par daalte hain aur codebase bhaari karte hain.

rule: Pin the Node version in a version file and package engines, and use the same version in CI.
why: Local aur CI mein alag version "mere machine par chalta hai" wale bugs lata hai.

practice: One package manager and a committed lockfile
rule: Use one package manager per repo, commit its lockfile and use clean installs in CI.
why: Do package managers ke lockfiles alag versions install kar dete hain.

rule: Use import aliases declared in one place instead of deep ../../ relative paths, with all source under one src folder.
why: Deep relative paths file move karte hi toot jate hain aur alag alias lists drift karti hain.

rule: Configuration files only read environment and return objects; no network calls or process exits.
why: Config mein side effects boot ko slow aur unpredictable banate hain.

practice: Check that a pattern is representative
rule: Before copying nearby code, confirm it matches the repository's majority pattern and choose deliberately when several coexist.
why: Qareeb wala code kabhi purana ya ghalat example hota hai.

rule: Before adopting a library, check how and which version the repository already uses and record any open version question.
why: Ek hi library ke do versions ya incompatible packages build tor dete hain.

rule: When nearby code contradicts the written standard, follow the standard and flag the discrepancy in the pull request.
why: Ghalat pattern copy karne se ghalti poore codebase mein phail jati hai.

rule: Start projects from a shared starter and new modules from a generator, and fix wrong shapes in the template, not only in the copy.
why: Haath se likhe modules har developer ke saath alag shakal le lete hain.

rule: Trace an unexpected null or wrong type to the code that produced it and fix it there, not with a guard in the consumer.
why: Consumer par patch asal bug ko zinda rakhta hai aur doosre clients phir bhi ghalat data paate hain.

rule: Delete an unwanted code path instead of hiding it behind a flag; use flags only for behaviour that truly varies at runtime.
why: Band flags wala dead code saalon tak confusion aur risk banata hai.

rule: Every handler runs: authenticate and authorize, rate limit before parsing, validate input, call one service, return the contract shape.
why: Ek jaisa order review ko tez aur security steps bhoolne ko mushkil banata hai.

rule: Keep a handler under roughly 40 lines; anything longer is hiding logic that belongs in a service.
why: Lamba handler business logic ka chhupa adda ban jata hai.

rule: Declare each endpoint on purpose with a validator and an auth check inside a guarded route group; never auto-generate CRUD from models.
why: Auto CRUD aur bhoole hue guards aisi cheezein expose karte hain jo kabhi public nahi honi chahiye.

rule: Validate every external input at the entry point for format, type and length.
why: Bina validation ka input injection aur crash dono ka darwaza hai.

rule: Define one schema per endpoint with a validation library such as zod; it is the only place the request shape is defined.
why: Haath ki checks har route mein alag aur adhoori hoti hain.

rule: Trim strings and cap string lengths, array lengths and upload sizes explicitly.
why: Bina limit ke bari payload memory aur database dono ko bhar deti hai.

rule: Detect an upload's type from its content bytes, not its file extension.
why: Extension badal kar khatarnak file upload karna bohat aasan hai.

rule: Every API error uses the same response shape, for example { error, code }, built by a shared helper.
why: Har endpoint ka alag error format client code ko bohat complex bana deta hai.

rule: Return 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 422 and 429 (with Retry-After) for known cases, and 5xx only for genuinely unexpected failures.
why: Ghalat status code client aur monitoring dono ko gumrah karta hai.

rule: A 500 returns a generic message; the real cause is logged server-side with a scope prefix.
why: Stack trace ya DB error attacker ko system ka naqsha de deta hai.

rule: Include useful context when re-throwing or propagating an error to a higher level.
why: Bina context ka error log se asal jagah dhoondna mushkil hota hai.

rule: Request and response types live in one module imported by both the server route and the client.
why: Do alag copies chupke se drift karti hain aur runtime par tootti hain.

rule: A route never returns a field the contract does not name.
why: Extra fields sensitive data leak aur undocumented dependency banate hain.

practice: Version and document public API changes
rule: Breaking public API changes get a version prefix and deprecation note, and docs are generated from the code and kept private unless the API is public.
why: Bina version ke change integrations tor deta hai aur alag likhe docs purane ho jate hain.

rule: All backend calls go through one client that attaches auth and headers, parses responses and returns typed errors.
why: Bikhre fetch calls mein auth aur error handling har jagah alag hoti hai.

rule: On a 401 the client clears session state once and routes to sign-in without retrying.
why: Retry loop expired session par server ko bekaar requests se bhar deta hai.

rule: Call third-party APIs through their official SDK rather than hand-written raw requests.
why: Raw requests mein retries, types aur error handling khud banana parta hai.

practice: One auth helper, explicit public routes
rule: Every page and handler resolves the caller through one shared auth helper, edge middleware is never the only check, and public routes say so.
why: Har route mein alag auth logic ho to kahin na kahin chhed reh jata hai.

rule: If authentication throws or a required secret is missing, the request is rejected, never allowed through.
why: Error par aage jane dena har route ko public bana deta hai.

rule: Login and reset responses are identical whether or not the account exists.
why: Mukhtalif response attacker ko valid emails ki list bana kar deta hai.

rule: Generate tokens and codes with a secure random generator and store only their hash; encrypt only values that must be shown again.
why: Database leak hone par bhi asal tokens istemal nahi ho sakte.

rule: Session cookies are httpOnly, secure, sameSite lax with an explicit maxAge, backed by rows with expiry and revocation so logout really ends them.
why: Ghalat flags ya na-revoke hone wale sessions churaye ja kar misuse hote hain.

rule: Hash passwords with scrypt or bcrypt and never serialize the hash column in responses.
why: Plain ya kamzor hash leak hone par saare passwords khul jate hain.

rule: Compare shared secrets and service keys with a timing-safe comparison, never plain equality.
why: Timing attack se secret harf harf guess kiya ja sakta hai.

practice: The client is never the authority
rule: Keep mobile tokens in secure storage, strip them from persisted state, and fetch roles and verification flags from the server each session.
why: Local flag badal kar user khud ko admin ya verified bana sakta hai.

rule: Confirm the caller may access each record, not only that they are signed in.
why: Sirf id badal kar doosre user ka data parhna (IDOR) sab se aam bug hai.

practice: Roles as one closed enum from a trusted source
rule: Define a small closed role enum in one file and read the role from the database or a verified token, never from the request.
why: Request mein role bhejna har user ko admin banne ki dawat hai.

practice: Scope every tenant query and channel
rule: Every tenant-scoped query and realtime channel filters by a tenant taken from the session, using one documented tenancy model.
why: Ek bhoola hua filter ek customer ka data doosre ko dikha deta hai.

rule: Return 401 for missing or invalid credentials and 403 for signed-in callers who are not allowed.
why: Ghalat code se client ghalat qadam uthata hai, jaise bekaar re-login.

rule: Put admin routes under one guarded group and record admin changes to customer data with who, what and when.
why: Naya admin route guard bhool jaye to sab ke liye khul jata hai aur bina audit ghalat change trace nahi hota.

rule: Derive plan features and limits from the subscription record on the server for each request; client-side limits are display only.
why: Client par bharosa karne se free user paid feature khol leta hai.

rule: Rate limit every endpoint that sends email or SMS, spends AI tokens or accepts credentials.
why: Bina limit ke bots bill barha dete hain aur passwords guess karte hain.

rule: Key limits by IP and by a hashed identity, store counters durably, and refuse rather than allow when the store is down in production.
why: Sirf IP ya in-memory counter restart aur VPN se bypass ho jata hai.

rule: For long or paid calls, reserve quota, run with a timeout below the platform limit, and refund on every failure path.
why: Timeout ya error par user ka quota bina kaam ke kat jata hai.

rule: Run recurring work as a secret-protected endpoint triggered by an external scheduler that prevents overlapping runs.
why: Process ke andar timers restart par gum hote hain aur overlapping runs data double karti hain.

rule: Every retryable side effect in a job (email, SMS, vendor call) carries an idempotency key.
why: Job dobara chale to customer ko do emails ya do charges nahi jate.

rule: Use one structured logger per repo and no console.log in application code.
why: Bikhre console logs production mein shor aur gum shuda info dono banate hain.

rule: Never log raw bodies, headers or query strings; mask secrets and personal data with one shared, tested scrubber.
why: Logs mein password, token ya PII leak hona aam aur khatarnak ghalti hai.

rule: Every request log line has a request id, route, status and duration, and messages carry a scope prefix.
why: Yeh fields na hon to slow ya failing request dhoondna mushkil hai.

rule: Report unexpected errors to an error tracking service someone watches, not console output alone.
why: Console mein gira error koi nahi dekhta jab tak user shikayat na kare.

rule: Name tables and columns in snake_case, with plural table names.
why: Mixed naming se queries mein quotes aur ghaltiyan barhti hain.

rule: Use identity integers for internal rows and UUIDs when the id appears in URLs.
why: URL mein sequential id se doosre records guess karna aasan hota hai.

practice: Timestamps everywhere, soft delete only when needed
rule: Every table has created_at and updated_at; add deleted_at only for restore or audit, and make every query respect it.
why: Bina timestamps debug mushkil aur adha soft delete deleted data wapas dikha deta hai.

practice: Closed sets are enums or checks
rule: Store statuses as an enum type or a CHECK constraint, never free text.
why: Free text status mein typos chupke se ghalat states bana dete hain.

rule: Declare every foreign key with a deliberate on delete action, and index foreign keys and filtered columns with predictable names.
why: Bina index ke queries slow aur bina FK ke orphan rows ban jati hain.

rule: Write one timestamped migration per change, named for what it does.
why: Bara mixed migration review aur rollback dono mushkil banata hai.

rule: Use if not exists, create or replace and guarded blocks, and verify by applying the migration twice.
why: Dobara chalne par fail hone wala migration deploy ko beech mein rok deta hai.

rule: Once a migration is merged, write a new migration instead of changing it.
why: Purana migration badalne se mukhtalif databases ki state alag ho jati hai.

rule: Run migrations from CI or the deploy step with a dry run on pull requests, never lazily from application code.
why: Request par schema banana do jagah schema aur race conditions lata hai.

rule: Every migration has a down path; destructive changes need a backup and human approval, and data backfills ship with a tested script.
why: Ek ghalat drop ya backfill production data hamesha ke liye kharab kar sakta hai.

practice: Generate row types from the schema
rule: Generate database types from the schema and derive request, response and domain shapes from them; never hand-write row types.
why: Haath ke types column rename ke baad bhi chupke se purane rehte hain.

rule: Regenerate and commit types in the same pull request as the migration, and have CI fail if they are stale.
why: Types aur schema alag hon to compile pass ho kar runtime fail hota hai.

practice: Invent types only for what the schema lacks
rule: Write a custom type only for shapes the schema does not describe, such as multi-table payloads.
why: Faltu duplicate types drift ka zariya bante hain.

rule: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database access.
why: String jor kar banayi query SQL injection ka seedha darwaza hai.

rule: When a column name must be dynamic, such as a sort field, map it through a fixed allow-list.
why: Column names parameterize nahi hote, is liye allow-list ke baghair injection mumkin hai.

practice: Queries only in the data layer
rule: All queries live in the data or service layer; routes, pages, components and controllers never build them.
why: Bikhri queries mein tenant filter aur performance control karna na-mumkin hai.

rule: Check and change a limited value in one statement, for example update where used < limit.
why: Alag read aur write ke beech race se limit cross ho jati hai.

practice: Size connection pools for the platform
rule: Keep pools small and reused on serverless; use framework defaults on long-lived servers and document any change.
why: Serverless par bare pools database connections khatam kar dete hain.

rule: No secret is ever committed, and .gitignore ignores all .env files except .env.example.
why: Git history se secret kabhi poori tarah nahi mitta.

rule: .env.example lists every variable name the app reads with a note on what breaks without it, and no values.
why: Naye developer ko pata nahi chalta kaunsi setting missing hai.

practice: Scan for secrets on commit and in CI
rule: Run a secret scanner in a pre-commit hook and in CI.
why: Galti se add hua key push se pehle pakra jata hai.

rule: When a secret leaks, rotate it first, then clean history, then confirm the old value no longer works.
why: History saaf karne se leak wapas nahi hota, sirf rotation bachata hai.

practice: Public env prefixes only for publishable keys
rule: Variables with a browser-public prefix hold only keys that are safe to ship to every user.
why: Public prefix wala secret har visitor ke browser mein pohanch jata hai.

rule: Mark modules that read secrets as server-only so an accidental client import fails the build.
why: Galti se secret client bundle mein chala jata hai aur sab ko dikhta hai.

rule: Set CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame protection and HSTS, and tighten CSP toward nonces over time.
why: Headers ke baghair XSS, clickjacking aur sniffing attacks aasan ho jate hain.

rule: Configure CORS origins and remote image hosts as explicit lists; never a wildcard origin with credentials.
why: Wildcard kisi bhi site ko user ki taraf se requests bhejne ya server ko proxy banane deta hai.

rule: Check uploads by magic bytes, cap their size, store them under random keys and serve them through a proxy with an opaque token.
why: Seedha bucket URL aur bina check upload malware aur data leak ka zariya hain.

rule: Never interpolate user input into SQL, shell or HTML; encode output for where it is rendered.
why: Bina encoding ke input injection aur XSS ban jata hai.

rule: Use established crypto libraries and secure randomness, and encrypt in transit with verified TLS, including to the database.
why: Ghar ki crypto ya bina verification TLS data ko parhne aur badalne ke liye khula chhorta hai.

rule: Grant only the permissions an operation needs for files, database connections and API scopes.
why: Zyada permission ka matlab breach hone par zyada nuqsan.

practice: No dynamic execution of untrusted input
rule: Never pass untrusted input to eval, dynamic imports or unsafe deserializers.
why: Dynamic code execution attacker ko server par apna code chalane deta hai.

rule: Never build file system paths from user input without sanitizing and restricting them.
why: ../ wala input server ki koi bhi file parh ya likh sakta hai.

rule: Never create or update records from the whole request body; validate into an allow-listed shape first.
why: Request mein role ya price field bhej kar user unhein badal sakta hai.

practice: Error handlers must not fail open
rule: An exception in security-critical code must deny access and never expose stack traces or skip auth.
why: Error par allow karna ek chhupa hua bypass hai.

practice: Review generated code for missing auth
rule: Explicitly check every route and resource operation for authentication and authorization, especially in AI-generated code.
why: Generated code aksar auth middleware aur ownership check bhool jata hai.

rule: Enable an automated dependency update bot with grouped weekly updates.
why: Purani dependencies mein known vulnerabilities khuli rehti hain.

rule: Pin versions through a committed lockfile and fix peer dependency conflicts instead of forcing installs.
why: Bina pin ya force install se breaking ya malicious code chupke se aa jata hai.

rule: Remove unused packages, keep one library per need, and avoid unmaintained packages for security-critical work.
why: Har faltu ya lawaris package attack surface aur bundle size barhata hai.

rule: Pin vendored scripts and CI tools by version or hash, verify checksums, and review scripts like code.
why: Badla hua third-party script supply chain attack ban jata hai.

rule: Workflows that run pull request code use the safe pull request trigger and a minimal permissions block.
why: Ghalat trigger fork ke code ko repo secrets tak pohancha deta hai.

practice: Keep state as deep as possible
rule: Keep state in the lowest component that needs it and lift it only when siblings share it.
why: Upar rakhi state bekaar re-renders aur ulajhe props lati hai.

rule: Every component handles loading, empty, error and disabled states, or documents why one does not apply.
why: Sirf happy path banana user ko khali ya toota screen dikhata hai.

rule: Render data lists with stable keys and virtualize lists longer than about 50 items.
why: Bina key ke state ghalat row mein chali jati hai aur lambi list slow hoti hai.

rule: Use one shared modal component that closes by close button, Escape and backdrop; never hand-roll overlays.
why: Haath ke bane overlays focus trap aur escape bhool jate hain.

rule: Use the App Router with server components by default; add the client directive only to small leaves, never to pages or layouts.
why: Poora page client par ho to bundle bhaari aur data leak ka risk barhta hai.

rule: For dynamic segments with a known set of values, pre-generate params and turn off dynamic params so unknown slugs return 404.
why: Warna har random URL render ho kar server waste karta hai.

practice: Separate server, browser and admin clients
rule: Keep server, browser and privileged admin database clients in separate files, with the admin one server-only.
why: Ek mixed client admin powers galti se browser tak le jata hai.

practice: Keep private pages out of search
rule: Routes that render private data set noindex in their metadata.
why: Search engine mein private pages index ho kar leak ho jate hain.

rule: Components use semantic color tokens and fixed named scales for spacing, radius, shadow and z-index; never raw hex values.
why: Raw values se theme ya dark mode badalna har file chhoona banata hai.

practice: One type scale and few weights
rule: Use one type scale and two or three weights; show hierarchy with size and weight, not color.
why: Bohat saare sizes aur colors se hierarchy samajh nahi aati.

practice: Reuse primitives and one icon family
rule: Check existing UI primitives before adding one, and use SVG icons from a single family, never emoji.
why: Near-duplicate components aur mixed icons UI ko be-tarteeb bana dete hain.

rule: Text meets 4.5:1 contrast (3:1 for large text and UI), and meaning or chart series is never shown by color alone.
why: Kam contrast aur sirf rang wala signal kamzor nazar aur color blind users ke liye ghayab hota hai.

rule: Every interactive element has a visible focus ring, keyboard order matches visual order, and icon-only controls have accessible names.
why: Focus ring ya naam ke baghair keyboard aur screen reader users raasta kho dete hain.

rule: Touch targets are at least 44 pt on iOS, 48 dp on Android and 24 px on web, and nothing essential is hover-only.
why: Chhote targets par ghalat tap aam hai aur touch par hover hota hi nahi.

rule: Give images dimensions or an aspect ratio, use modern formats and lazy-load below-the-fold media.
why: Load hote waqt content kood kar user ghalat jagah click karta hai.

rule: Design mobile first with 16 px minimum body text, 1.5 line height, no horizontal scroll and dynamic viewport height units.
why: Desktop-only design phone par toota aur chhota nazar aata hai.

rule: Before designing or reviewing a screen, write its one job in one sentence, then measure it at a desktop and a phone viewport.
why: Do kaam wali screen ko koi layout fix theek nahi kar sakta aur andaze ka review behas banta hai.

rule: At most one primary-styled button is visible in any viewport; other actions are secondary or links.
why: Kai barabar buttons user ko confuse karte hain ke agla qadam kya hai.

rule: The answer to the screen's job starts in the first viewport, and banners, promos and onboarding together take at most 25 percent of it.
why: Fold ke neeche wali cheez par bohat kam tawajjo jati hai.

rule: Use a fixed spacing scale, make gaps between groups at least twice the gaps inside, add borders last and nest surfaces at most two deep.
why: Barabar spacing aur card ke andar card screen ko be-tarteeb aur bhaari banate hain.

rule: To reduce clutter, shrink, then collapse, then move, and remove last, keeping disclosure at most two levels deep.
why: Seedha delete zaroori cheez gira deta hai aur teen level deep cheez koi nahi dhoondta.

rule: Use at most three content text sizes plus the title and two large elements, and check that the primary element reads first in a blurred screenshot.
why: Bohat saari emphasis se aankh ko pata nahi chalta pehle kya dekhe.

rule: Headings start with the key word and stay under six words, with at most one line of description.
why: Users scan karte hain, pehle lafz mein matlab na ho to woh aage nikal jate hain.

practice: Every field has a named use
rule: Before a field ships, name who uses the answer and for what, and keep checkout to at most 8 fields.
why: Har faltu field form chhorne walon ki tadad barhata hai.

practice: One thing per page, one column
rule: Use one question per page for infrequent or branching flows and stack fields in a single column.
why: Lamba ya do column form users ko confuse kar ke fields skip karwata hai.

rule: Every field has a visible label; a placeholder is never the only label.
why: Typing shuru hote hi placeholder gayab ho kar user bhool jata hai field kya thi.

rule: Validate when the user leaves a field and on submit, never while they are still typing.
why: Har keystroke par error user ko ghabra deta hai.

rule: Errors are one sentence telling the user what to do, shown at the field and in a linked summary on submit, without clearing input.
why: "Invalid input" se user ko pata nahi chalta theek kaise kare aur kahan.

rule: Prefill values the system already knows and hide questions that do not apply.
why: Wohi cheez dobara poochna user ka waqt zaya karta hai.

rule: Buttons say verb plus object such as "Save and continue", and submit is disabled only while a request is in flight.
why: "Submit" ya bina wajah grey button user ko nahi batata ke kya hoga ya kya missing hai.

rule: Ask for confirmation before any destructive action.
why: Ek ghalat click se data delete ho jana user ka bharosa tor deta hai.

rule: Define one measurable value moment, keep the path to it short, and do not demand an account before users see value.
why: Value tak der se pohanchne wale users wapas nahi aate.

rule: A setup checklist has 3 to 5 items, opens only the next step, and shows "x of n done".
why: Lambi ya poori khuli checklist bohat kam log poori karte hain.

rule: Steps observable in data tick themselves automatically; manual self-report is only a secondary fallback.
why: User se jhoota ya bhoola hua self-report progress ko ghalat dikhata hai.

rule: Give onboarding less space as the account fills, celebrate completion once, and keep it hidden across sessions once dismissed.
why: Har login par wapas aane wali checklist asal kaam ki jagah kha jati hai.

rule: Every empty widget shows its final frame, one line on what will appear and at most one action to fill it.
why: Khali screen user ko yeh nahi batati ke agla qadam kya hai.

rule: No modal or guard stops users from reaching the main screens; long setup moves to its own route instead.
why: Zabardasti tour users ko naraz karta hai aur performance nahi barhata.

rule: The first screen shows what needs attention, how things are going and what to do next, with the top priority at top left.
why: Bina tarteeb dashboard mein zaroori alert neeche dab jata hai.

practice: At most four stat cards in one row
rule: Show at most one row of up to four stat cards, each with a label, value, delta and comparison period.
why: Bohat saare numbers mein koi bhi number ahem nahi lagta.

rule: Compare quantities with bars or lines; avoid pie, donut, gauge and 3D charts.
why: Insaan angle aur area ka sahi andaza nahi laga pata.

rule: Tables use a readable first column, right-aligned numbers, a sticky header and at most two visible row actions.
why: Id pehle ho aur har row par icons ka dher ho to table scan nahi hota.

rule: Loading, empty and error states keep the widget's final size, errors show per widget with retry, and a failure never looks like "No data".
why: Page kood jaye ya failure khali lage to user ghalat faisla karta hai.

rule: Use inline indicators for element status, toasts only for passive success, and modals only for consequential decisions.
why: Toast mein error ghayab ho jata hai aur user ko pata hi nahi chalta.

rule: Animate only transform and opacity, never width, height or layout properties.
why: Layout animate karna jank aur slow frames paida karta hai.

rule: Every animation expresses cause and effect, exits are shorter than entrances, and animations can be interrupted.
why: Bekaar animation sirf user ka waqt leti hai aur distract karti hai.

rule: Honour the user's reduced-motion preference.
why: Kuch users ko animation se chakkar ya takleef hoti hai.

rule: Take every duration from one small named token scale and use one shared easing curve without bounce.
why: Har file mein alag timing aur curves app ko be-jor mehsoos karwate hain.

practice: Compare at real size, match the reference
rule: Compare design alternatives side by side at the target viewport with the same data, and list every deliberate departure from a reference.
why: Thumbnail par acha layout asal size par fail hota hai aur bina bataye drift design ko bigarta hai.

practice: Checks pass locally and in CI
rule: A change is done only when typecheck, lint and format pass locally and in CI.
why: Local par skip kiye checks CI mein waqt zaya karte hain ya main tor dete hain.

practice: Changed branching logic has a unit test
rule: Every changed pure function with branching has a unit test.
why: Bina test ki branch agle change mein chupke se toot jati hai.

practice: Config and docs updated with the change
rule: New environment variables go into .env.example and changed behaviour updates the docs, in the same change.
why: Purane docs aur missing settings agle developer ya deploy ko fail karte hain.

rule: UI changes include a screenshot and are checked at phone and desktop widths, by keyboard alone and in both themes.
why: Reviewer code se UI ka asar nahi dekh sakta aur doosre devices par toota UI chhup jata hai.

rule: A change is not done until a reviewer other than the author approves it.
why: Apni ghalti khud ko nazar nahi aati.

rule: Cover parsers, validators, token helpers, calculations and scrubbers with fast pure unit tests.
why: Yeh sab se sasta aur tez test hai jo zyada bugs pakarta hai.

rule: Tests never touch production or shared staging data; use a disposable container or isolated project.
why: Test ne production data mita diya, yeh kahani bohat aam hai.

rule: Replace external vendors with fakes in tests so CI needs no real credentials.
why: Real vendor se test slow, flaky aur mehnga hota hai.

rule: Keep paid AI calls out of CI; use a free contract test and an on-demand evaluation with a cost estimate.
why: Har push par paid calls ka bill tezi se barhta hai.

rule: Flows like billing or account opening keep a written manual test playbook run and logged before each release.
why: Kuch flows automate karna mushkil hai aur ghalti ka asar wapas nahi hota.

rule: Every endpoint has tests for success, each validation failure, auth failures that leak nothing, and limits at their boundary.
why: Sirf happy path test karne se security aur validation bugs chhup jate hain.

rule: Test and approve an endpoint before any frontend code calls it.
why: Toote API par bana frontend dobara banana parta hai.

rule: Tests sign in as a seeded account with a confirmed email so authorization and scoping apply exactly as in production.
why: Auth bypass kar ke test karna asal permission bugs nahi pakarta.

rule: A test bypass is read from a secret, refused in production, skips only one interactive gate, and has a unit test proving it.
why: Dheela bypass asal mein ek backdoor ban jata hai.

rule: Optimize only after profiling identifies a measurable bottleneck, not during initial development.
why: Andaze se optimize karna ghalat jagah waqt lagata hai aur code ulajhata hai.

rule: Fix algorithmic complexity and pick data structures by access pattern before micro-optimizing lines.
why: O(n^2) loop ko chhoti tweaks kabhi tez nahi karti.

rule: Close and release memory, connections and file handles properly.
why: Leak hone wale resources server ko dheere dheere gira dete hain.

practice: Push over polling for live data
rule: Deliver live data through server-sent events or sockets from one listener module; poll only as a documented last resort.
why: Polling server load barhata hai aur data phir bhi late aata hai.

rule: Never commit directly to main; nothing merges without a green pipeline and an approval.
why: Direct commit review aur CI bypass karta hai aur toota main poori team ko rokta hai.

rule: Name branches type/kebab-summary such as feat/ or fix/, keep them short-lived and delete them on merge.
why: Lambi chalne wali branches conflicts barhati hain aur purani branches confusion.

rule: Write each commit message as one short line under 72 characters saying what changed and why.
why: Lamba ya "fixes" jaisa message history ko bekaar bana deta hai.

rule: Commit at each meaningful checkpoint while the code still works.
why: Ek bara commit review aur revert dono mushkil banata hai.

rule: Squash or amend only on an unpushed branch you alone own, and never collapse a repository's history into one commit.
why: Shared history badalne se doosron ka kaam aur har faisle ki wajah mit jati hai.

rule: Stage your own files by path instead of adding everything, especially on shared working trees.
why: Sab add karna doosre ka adhoora kaam ya secrets commit kar deta hai.

rule: Run lint and format on staged files in a pre-commit hook and never bypass hooks without an explicit reason.
why: Hook skip karna wohi ghaltiyan main tak pohanchata hai.

rule: Open every pull request from the template, link its task, fill each section and delete sections that do not apply.
why: Adhoori description reviewer ko andhere mein chhorti hai.

rule: Keep a pull request under about 400 changed lines; split bigger work into a stack.
why: Bari PR ko log sarsari review kar ke approve kar dete hain.

rule: Merge only when CI is green: typecheck, lint, format, build, tests, secret scan and migration check.
why: Laal CI ke saath merge toota code main mein le aata hai.

rule: Require approval from someone other than the author, and from an owner for auth, billing, migration or deploy changes.
why: Sensitive areas mein akeli nazar bari ghalti chhor deti hai.

rule: Review within one working day or hand it off, and reply to every comment; "done" is fine, silence is not.
why: Rukay hue PRs aur bina jawab comments conflicts aur confusion barhate hain.

rule: Read the description before the diff, then check every mutation for authorization and every query for tenant scoping.
why: Wajah jaane bina review sirf style par hota hai aur bara data leak miss ho jata hai.

rule: Block only for correctness, security or standards, and write comments as one short instruction with the fix as code.
why: Lambi behas aur har pasand par block team ko slow karta hai.

rule: Every pull request runs install, secret scan, typecheck, lint and format with zero warnings, build, migration check and tests.
why: Har stage ek alag qisam ki ghalti merge se pehle pakarti hai.

rule: CI uses the project's pinned runtime version and its workflow files live in the repository root workflow folder.
why: Alag version ya nested workflow folder ki wajah se tests ya to ghalat chalte hain ya chalte hi nahi.

rule: Every product has production plus a preview or staging lane, each with its own database, and pull requests get preview deploys.
why: Shared database mein staging ka test production data kharab kar deta hai.

practice: App environment separate from build mode
rule: Use a dedicated app environment variable (local, staging, production) separate from the build mode, validated at boot.
why: Build mode se environment guess karna staging aur production ko mix kar deta hai.

practice: Build once, deploy atomically after tests
rule: Deploy only after tests pass, build one artifact, and switch to a new release instead of deleting the live one first.
why: Pehle delete kar ke deploy fail ho to site band ho jati hai.

rule: Keep a docs/knowledge folder with a short manifest, a newcomer reading order, and one bounded question per doc.
why: Bina index ke docs bikhar jate hain aur koi parhta nahi.

rule: Record non-obvious decisions, including what was deliberately not built, as dated one-line entries in a decisions log.
why: Wajah likhi na ho to log same faisla baar baar dobara kholte hain.

rule: Record each trap with its symptom, cause and fix, and keep a one-line glossary wherever the domain has jargon.
why: Har naya developer wohi trap mein phans kar din zaya karta hai.

rule: Update the doc that describes changed behaviour in the same pull request and track the commit each doc was last verified against.
why: Baad mein docs update karna aksar hota hi nahi aur purana doc ghalat rasta dikhata hai.

practice: No secrets or personal data in docs
rule: Docs may name variables and secrets but never contain their values or personal data.
why: Docs aksar sab ke saath share hote hain, wahan secret leak ho jata hai.

rule: Write absolute dates, fix or delete wrong docs, and keep one documentation tree instead of a second doc on the same question.
why: Stale knowledge koi knowledge na hone se bhi zyada nuqsan karti hai.

rule: Keep one short agent instructions file at the repo root that tool-specific files import instead of duplicating.
why: Do files mein rules duplicate hon to woh alag ho jate hain.

practice: Plan first, then stay in scope
rule: An agent proposes its approach before building and stops when the task ends, reporting adjacent work instead of starting it.
why: Ghalat samjhi requirement aur scope creep ka kaam phenkna parta hai ya systems ko nuqsan deta hai.

practice: Explicit ask for every push or merge
rule: An agent pushes, merges or opens a pull request only when the current request explicitly asks for it.
why: Purani hidayat ko standing permission samajhna unreviewed code push kar deta hai.

rule: Agents never write to a live backend and apply only non-destructive, idempotent, reversible migrations themselves.
why: Agent ki ek ghalat query production data mita sakti hai.

practice: Never claim a safety net you did not create
rule: Only mention a backup, tag or stash that actually exists and has been verified.
why: Jhoota recovery point koi recovery point na hone se bhi bura hai.

practice: Do not touch others' uncommitted work
rule: On a shared tree, avoid stash, reset, path checkout, clean and amend that can take or destroy another person's changes.
why: Ek agent ka stash doosre ka kaam gayab kar deta hai.

practice: Agents verify in code, humans verify visually
rule: Agents use the existing dev server and verify with typecheck, lint and tests, then give the human a short list of what to look at.
why: Agent ke apne servers purana build serve karte hain aur browser chalana sessions ko khatre mein dalta hai.

rule: Agents read secret files only when needed, never print or commit secrets, and committed settings grant no broad permissions.
why: Chat ya logs mein aaya secret leak samjha jata hai aur broad permission khatarnak kaam karwati hai.

practice: Leave a handoff, not hidden memory
rule: End a session with a handoff note of what changed and what is next, and never let agent memory override written standards.
why: Agla session andhere mein shuru hota hai aur purani memory ghalat rule zinda rakhti hai.

rule: Expose a health endpoint that checks config and a database round trip, returns 503 on failure, and is polled after every deploy.
why: Bina health check toota deploy chupke se live reh kar users ko errors deta hai.

rule: Jobs that spend money check a kill-switch setting before doing work and are idempotent.
why: Loop mein phansa job raaton raat bara bill bana deta hai.

rule: Provide a one-command idempotent seed script with no real customer data that refuses to run in production.
why: Seed production par chal jaye ya real data rakhe to bara nuqsan ho sakta hai.

rule: On a leaked secret or auth bypass, stop feature work, rotate or fix, and report what leaked and what was rotated the same day.
why: Der se response leak ko aur bara nuqsan karne deta hai.
